<reason>PRO kept the land-scarce arithmetic live - recurring deaths vs finite land - while CON conceded forever was never literal. PRO's turn that reuse admits permanence is finished and disturbs undisturbed graves worse than the motion damaged CON's smarter-burial and religious routes, which CON never solved with exempt sections still consuming hectares. CON's pluralism and visiting-place pressure was real but PRO answered with groves/columbaria and honest equal service.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's reuse-as-confession in R1 sharpened in R2 A1: if graves are reclaimed when memory fades permanence is already surrendered, and reclaiming violates Jewish/Muslim undisturbed-grave duty worse than composting/hydrolysis, leaving CON defending delay at hectares of cost.</best_rebuttal>
